title: SG-5.5 · Scheduler behavior with a fake clock unit tests
summary: Unit tests prove Scheduler.Tick opens due rounds, closes expired rounds, waits for boundaries and keeps going after an Open error
description: Context: backend/internal/round/scheduler.go already implements Scheduler.Tick with an injected Clock, Controller and Lister. backend/internal/round/scheduler_test.go already holds tests using fakeClock, fakeController and fakeLister. Desired behavior: the four named scheduler behaviors are covered by passing unit tests that use only fakes. Expected result: go test for those tests passes. Why: the round lifecycle must open and close rounds on time without a real clock.
acceptance_criteria: Given a SCHEDULED round whose StartsAt is before the fake clock time, when Tick runs, then Controller.Open is called once for that round and Close is not called
Given an OPEN round whose EndsAt is before the fake clock time, when Tick runs, then Controller.Close is called once for that round

Given future-start SCHEDULED, future-end OPEN and COMPLETED rounds, when Tick runs before the boundary, then no Controller call is made, and when the clock reaches the boundary, then only the due Open and Close calls are made
Given Controller.Open returns an error and another round is due for Close, when Tick runs, then Tick returns an error wrapping the Open error and Close is still called for the other round

in_scope: Scheduler.Tick behavior with a fake clock
out_of_scope: Real Controller, store or Git behavior
preserve: Scheduler, Clock, Controller and Lister public signatures

technical_constraints: No real clock, sleep, filesystem or network in the tests
definition_of_done: All four Tick behaviors are asserted by passing unit tests
